title: Isolation of myenteric and submucosal plexus from mouse gastrointestinal tract and subsequent flow cytometry and immunofluorescence
protocol: Euthanize mouse by cervical dislocation or other approved method.
Lay euthanized mouse on its back on a cold surface.
Spray abdominal area with 70% ethanol.
Make a V-shaped incision in the skin of the lower abdomen with scissors.
Cut away skin to expose abdominal cavity.
Locate the beginning of the small intestine at the base of the stomach.
Cut the beginning of the small intestine from the stomach and carefully pull it out from the abdominal cavity.
Allow mesenteric fat to peel away from the intestine as it is pulled.
Gently remove remaining fat with tweezers.
Divide the small intestine into four equal pieces.
Collect the ileum, which is the most distal fourth of the small intestinal tissue proximal to the beginning of the cecum.
Insert scissors into intestinal opening.
Carefully pull intestine over scissor blade.
Make a straight cut to the right of the mesenteric attachment over the length of the tissue until intestine is fully opened.
Locate the outside layer of the intestine (the smooth side with mesenteric attachment).
Grip with tweezers and vigorously shake in a petri dish filled with PBS on ice to wash.
Place the intestine on a cold surface with the muscularis (outer) layer facing up (luminal side facing down).
Use small, damp paint brushes to completely flatten the tissue, making sure the sides don’t fold under.
Grip the intestine at the beginning of the tissue segment using one pair of tweezers.
Make a dent in the tissue directly below the gripping point without piercing through the entire thickness.
Stroke downwards on the tissue from the indentation with the second pair of tweezers until layers separate and the muscularis rolls away.
Gradually adjust both pairs of tweezers down the length of the tissue, scraping the muscularis layer away until reaching the end of the tissue segment.
Store the tissue in PBS on ice until all animals are processed.
Place tissue on a Sylgard-coated plate.
Stretch and flatten the tissue using damp paint brushes, avoiding wrinkles or folds.
Pin down the flattened tissue with Minutien pins.
Cover pinned tissue with 4% PFA solution.
Keep tissue in PFA at 4°C for 16 h.
Discard PFA solution and transfer tissue to a 24-well plate filled with PBS.
Wash tissue four times for 15 min per wash on an orbital shaker, transferring to fresh wells after each wash.
Transfer tissue to 24-well plate filled with Permeabilization Buffer.
Incubate tissue in Permeabilization Buffer at 20°C–25°C on an orbital shaker for 2 h, moving to a second PBS-filled well after 1 h.
Pause point: Tissue can be kept in Permeabilization Buffer at 4°C for up to 1 week.
For longer storage (2 months), secure the plate with parafilm and keep tissue in Permeabilization Buffer supplemented with 0.05% sodium azide.
Transfer tissue to a 24-well plate filled with Blocking Buffer.
Incubate at 20°C–25°C on an orbital shaker for 1 h.
Prepare 600 μL of primary antibody solution per 4 cm piece of muscularis, diluted in Blocking Buffer.
Place tissue in antibody solution in a 24-well plate; seal with parafilm and incubate for 48 h at 4°C on a platform rocker.
Transfer tissue to a 24-well plate filled with PBS.
Wash 4 times for 15 min per wash at 20°C–25°C on an orbital shaker, transferring tissue to a new PBS-filled well after each wash.
Prepare 600 μL of secondary antibody solution per 4 cm piece of muscularis, diluted in Permeabilization Buffer.
Incubate tissue in solution in a 24-well plate for 2–3 h at 20°C–25°C, covered from light on an orbital shaker.
Transfer tissue to a 24-well plate filled with PBS.
Wash 4 times for 15 min per wash at 20°C–25°C on an orbital shaker, transferring tissue to a new PBS-filled well after each wash.
Transfer tissue to a microscope slide.
Completely flatten with damp paint brushes.
Cover with a few drops of Fluoromount-G mounting medium and carefully place a coverslip on the tissue sample.
Avoid introducing air bubbles by lowering the coverslip gradually from one side to the other.
Allow slides to dry for 16 h in dark at 20°C–25°C, or until the media solidifies.
Acquire 10 randomly selected, evenly spaced, complete z-stacks for each slide.
Remove Peyer’s patches from tissue using scissors or tweezers.
Cut tissue thoroughly into very fine pieces (less than 0.5 mm) in a 6-well plate without liquid.
Add Digestion Buffer to the well and place on a shaker at 37°C.
Incubate muscularis for 40 min with 4 mL of Digestion Buffer.
Incubate mucosae for 20 min with 6 mL of Digestion Buffer.
Homogenize tissue with an 18G needle/10 mL syringe by aspirating up and down twice.
Add 5 mL HBSS+5% FCS to each well.
Filter the cell suspension through a 70 μm cell strainer directly into a 15 mL falcon tube using a 10 mL serological pipet.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 400 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Aspirate supernatant and resuspend pellet in 100 μL of FACS buffer.
Transfer cells to a round-bottom 96-well plate using a pipette.
Centrifuge plate at 400 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Remove supernatant by quickly inverting the plate over the sink.
Resuspend cells in 50 μL of surface antibody mix diluted in FACS buffer.
Incubate for 30 min on ice, covered from light.
Wash cells by adding 100 μL of FACS buffer to each well.
Centrifuge plate at 400 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Remove supernatant by quickly inverting the plate over the sink.
Optional: Make Fix/Perm Buffer by diluting 1 part Fix/Perm Concentrate in 3 parts Fix/Perm Diluent.
Resuspend cells in 50 μL of Fix/Perm Buffer and incubate for 30 min on ice, covered from light.
Wash cells by adding 100 μL of Perm buffer to each well.
Centrifuge at 400 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Remove supernatant by quickly inverting the plate over the sink.
Resuspend cells in 50 μL of intracellular antibody mix diluted in Perm buffer (diluted 1:10 in water).
Wash cells by adding 100 μL of Perm buffer to each well.
Centrifuge at 400 g for 5 min at 4°C.
Remove supernatant by quickly inverting the plate over the sink.
Resuspend cells in 300 μL of FACS buffer and transfer to FACS tubes.
Acquire samples on FACS machine.
